interface: docs/scripts/reference-harness.mjs (sdkGuides manifest section, receipt.sdkGuides, sdkGate option)

gate.enforcedWhen: the release lane turns the gate on when the first producing node (XSDK9) supplies executable SDK examples; until then every slot stays pending and the standard docs check runs without the gate
gate.rule: every topic must be supplied by a manifest example whose files include a file with an executable source extension (.ts/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs) and whose entry is a shipped-bin command or a public import; a static sample manifest without an executable extension, a pending topic, or an unbound slot fails the gate

uncertaintyNotes: The SDK guide model requires actual SDK examples when the producing nodes land; today all six slots are pending and no page claims a working SDK example. Executable here means an executable source file plus a shipped-bin command or public import, validated statically; runtime execution of examples stays with the later executable-journey and SDK tooling nodes.
permissions: the harness reads the repository and spawns the existing typeinfo freshness command; the sdk gate adds no new process, network or write permission
migrationNotes: additive to the DOC1 harness and the examples/reference manifest. Editors' shipped pages under docs/editor remain the official-extension truth; topic pages link them and never restate a capability matrix. XSDK9 migrates slots from pending to supplied by binding example ids in manifest.json sdkGuides and turning on --sdk-gate in the release lane.
resourceRationale: synchronous static validation over a small authored tree; no new latency, allocation or RSS budget is bound to the ratified performance methodology
